category.introContent:
Thanks to quickly advancing technologies, hearing aids have become more sophisticated, capable, and discreet in recent years. About 37.5 million adults in the United States have hearing loss to some degree and would benefit from wearing hearing aids, but only 1 in 5 does so.

Research shows that helping to restore a person’s hearing can greatly improve their overall well-being and help them participate in everyday life with greater confidence and happiness. 

Picking the right hearing aid for your needs is no easy feat. To find the best hearing aids, we scored each brand according to their average price, range of models, features on offer and comfort. Our reviews will provide you with all the information you need to find the right hearing aid for you.

faqs.question: What is a premium hearing aid?
faqs.answer: Premium hearing aids include the most features for a seamless listening experience. These are best for individuals who live an active lifestyle and are in noisy environments often. This level of technology provides the most dynamic and automatic support in all types of listening situations.

faqs.question: Can you wear just 1 hearing aid?
faqs.answer: Can you wear just 1 hearing aid? If you have normal hearing in one ear, and mild hearing loss in the other, you're probably fine to just wear one hearing aid—just remember to get regular hearing tests to make sure your "good ear" is still hearing well

faqs.question: Do cheaper hearing aids work?
faqs.answer: Simply put, no — cheap hearing aids are not nearly as good as hearing aids you buy from an experienced hearing healthcare professional who is also adept at fitting and servicing these devices.

faqs.question: Does your hearing get worse if you don't wear hearing aid?
faqs.answer: For those experiencing hearing loss, many often wonder if their hearing gets worse if they don't wear a hearing aid. If you have hearing loss and have been advised to wear a hearing aid, the rate at which your hearing deteriorates will not be affected whether you wear the hearing aid or not.

category.bottomContent:
How does a hearing aid work?

Hearing aids are small electronic devices that are worn in or behind the ear by people with hearing loss. Their job is to amplify specific sounds helping their wearer hear and communicate with others better. These devices can improve hearing in both quiet and noisy environments, depending on the user’s specific needs.  

While there is a large range of designs available, almost all hearing aids function on the same basic principle. The hearing aid’s microphone picks up sound waves, converts them to electrical signals, and sends them to an amplifier. The amplifier then processes, boosts, and modifies the power of these signals and passes them on to a tiny receiver in the ear. 

Did you know? Only about one out of five people who would benefit from a hearing aid actually use one.

What are the different types of hearing aids available? 

Depending on the characteristics of your hearing loss, your ear, nose, and throat doctor (ENT) or audiology professional will recommend the right type of hearing aid for your needs.

Behind-the-ear (BTE)

A BTE hearing aid has two parts: the main part hooks over your ear and sits behind your auricle. A thin, clear tube connects it to a plastic earmold that fits inside the outer ear. The earpiece itself can be custom molded, but many people now use small pre-made ear tips that fit very comfortably within the ear canal.

Receiver-in-canal (RIC, also RITE)

The receiver-in-canal (RIC) and receiver-in-the-ear (RITE) styles are similar to a behind-the-ear hearing aid with the speaker or receiver that sits in the ear canal. A tiny wire, rather than tubing, connects the piece behind the ear to the speaker or receiver. This style of hearing aid usually has a less visible behind-the-ear portion and may be available with a rechargeable battery.

Completely-in-the-canal or invisible-in-the-canal(CIC/IIC)

A completely-in-the-canal(CIC) or invisible-in-the-canal (IIC) aid sits deeper inside the ear canal, making it nearly or entirely invisible. They are made to fit the size and shape of a person’s ear canal and are the most discreet kind of hearing aid. Because of their small size, these devices may be difficult for a person to adjust and remove. Their compact form also means less space for additional features such as volume control or extra microphones.

In-the-canal (ITC)/In-the-ear (ITE)

An in the ear/canal (ITE/ITC) aid sits completely within your outer ear (ITE) or just inside your ear canal (ITC). As these styles are larger than CIC/ICC hearing aids, they can include more practical features and are available with directional microphones (two microphones for better hearing in noise). ITE hearing aids usually include larger batteries than CIC/IIC models and can be easier to handle.

What you must consider before buying a hearing aid

Audiologist vs. direct-to-consumer

Hearing aids can be prescribed, programmed, and fitted by a licensed audiologist or ordered directly from the manufacturers. Direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands are generally less expensive, but you will sacrifice the benefits a local expert provides, including personalized device programming, in-depth hearing test results, and in-person customer service.

Hearing test

Before getting a prescription for hearing aids from a licensed audiologist, the first thing they will require is a thorough hearing test and evaluation. They will also explain the differences between hearing aid styles and recommend which type might fit your lifestyle best. Hearing tests are easy and painless and covered by most health insurance companies. Many online hearing aid retailers also include a free hearing test in their offer, so be sure to shop around. While you can order direct-to-consumer hearing aids without a hearing test, it is better to have as much information on your hearing loss as possible to inform your purchase decision.

Pricing

Unlike a hearing test, hearing aids are generally not covered by health insurance companies, leaving you to cover the cost. Hearing aid prices can vary significantly from retailer to retailer and range from just a few hundred dollars to well over $2000. Professional fees, remote controls, hearing aid accessories, and other hearing aid options may cost extra. Talk to your audiologist about your needs and expectations, and make sure that you understand which features are important to you and fit your budget. Almost all online hearing aid retailers offer comfortable payment plans to fit your financial needs.

Trial period 

Hearing aids can be a major investment, so make sure to purchase devices that come with a risk-free trial of at least 30 days, as well as a manufacturer’s warranty. Retailers will usually credit the cost of the trial toward the final price of the hearing aid. Also, ask how much of the purchase price is refundable if you return the hearing aid during the trial period.

Warranties/repairs and adjustments

Make sure your hearing aid includes a warranty that covers parts and labor for a specified period. Some hearing aid dispensers may include office visits or professional services such as cleanings and adjustments in the warranty.

Are additional accessories available?

Modern hearing aids, especially higher-end models, can come with a wide array of additional accessories such as remote controls, replaceable batteries, custom ear tips, cleaning tools, and many more. While some of these accessories are simply nice to have, others can make life with your new hearing aid considerably more comfortable.   

Extra features

Directional microphones 

Directional microphones help to improve the pickup of sounds and are most effective in noisy environments, allowing their wearer to focus on sounds from a specific direction without the distraction of background noise. Adaptive directional microphones can automatically focus on speech and sound coming from different directions giving their wearer the freedom to move between environments with varying noise levels comfortably.

Noise reduction/cancellation

All modern hearing aids have noise reduction features available. The degree of noise reduction will depend on the model of your hearing aid, with more expensive devices offering more advanced reduction. Some hearing aids also offer wind noise reduction.

Rechargeable batteries

Higher-end hearing aids have rechargeable batteries, making maintenance easier for you by eliminating the need to regularly change the battery. Keep in mind that these batteries are not usually replaceable, so when they reach the end of their lifespan (usually within 3-5 years), the hearing aids will need to be replaced.

Smartphone capabilities

Some modern hearing aids can wirelessly connect with your smartphone devices so you can stream calls and audio from your phone to your hearing aids. They also connect to hearing aid apps, allowing you to adjust your sound settings discreetly.

Takeaway

Hearing aids can be expensive, and while they are not usually covered by insurance or Medicare, companies do offer ways to spread out the costs. If you are willing to sacrifice some of the fancier features available in newer models, there are basic devices that are more affordable, yet still effective. We’ve broken down the top choices to help you find the best hearing aid for your needs.

Check out our in-depth reviews for more details.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is a premium hearing aid?+-

Premium hearing aids include the most features for a seamless listening experience. These are best for individuals who live an active lifestyle and are in noisy environments often. This level of technology provides the most dynamic and automatic support in all types of listening situations.

Can you wear just 1 hearing aid?+-

Can you wear just 1 hearing aid? If you have normal hearing in one ear, and mild hearing loss in the other, you're probably fine to just wear one hearing aid—just remember to get regular hearing tests to make sure your "good ear" is still hearing well

Do cheaper hearing aids work?+-

Simply put, no — cheap hearing aids are not nearly as good as hearing aids you buy from an experienced hearing healthcare professional who is also adept at fitting and servicing these devices.

Does your hearing get worse if you don't wear hearing aid?+-

For those experiencing hearing loss, many often wonder if their hearing gets worse if they don't wear a hearing aid. If you have hearing loss and have been advised to wear a hearing aid, the rate at which your hearing deteriorates will not be affected whether you wear the hearing aid or not.

Jabra Enhance Hearing Aid Models

Jabra Enhance offers high-quality, FDA-approved Bluetooth hearing aids. There are three models, the Enhance Select 300, Enhance Select 500, and Enhance Select 50R. The Enhance Select 300, Enhance Select 500, and Enhance Select 50R are rechargeable. All three function as behind-the-ear hearing aids, with a clever design that makes them virtually invisible when worn correctly.

The Jabra Enhance brand is known for its cutting-edge technology and excellent quality. All products come with a 3-year warranty, 3-year loss and damage protection, and 3 years of care from the company’s expert audiology team. You can also select from 8 different device colors, and it’s recommended that you match the color of your hearing aids to your hair color.

Rechargeable

The rechargeable Enhance Select 300 hearing aids come with a 100-day risk free trial and the Enhance Select 500 being from$1,795, which is a little expensive compared to some alternatives. However, the audiologist care and other inclusions mean that there’s actually great value for money here.

All rechargeable hearing aids come with a charging case that holds 3 full charges worth of power, enabling you to maintain fully charged hearing aids in all situations. It takes around 3 hours to charge a pair of hearing aids, and a full charge should last for around 30 hours.

There’s a mobile app that you can use to fine-tune your device, and you will have access to 24/7 support from the company’s Care Team. Other standout features include cutting-edge hearing aid technology. This includes background noise-cancelling, Bluetooth connectivity, and automatic voice recognition.

Jabra Enhance Additional Services & Products

There’s a selection of accessories available to help you get the most out of your Jabra Enhance hearing aids. A TV streamer is available for $299, which is designed to stream audio from your television and other devices to your hearing aids, enabling a much better hearing experience.

The MultiMic device ($275) is a small portable microphone that’s designed to stream sound to your aids in situations where listening is difficult, such as in restaurants or at events. Replacement charging cases cost $250 each, and the Android Phone Clip+ ($199) is designed to stream audio from older Bluetooth devices to your hearing aids.

How Do I Purchase Jabra Enhance Devices?

Purchasing Jabra Enhance devices is quite a simple process, although there’s more to it than simply adding them to your cart and completing the checkout process. First, you will need to take an online hearing test.

A qualified hearing specialist will program your hearing aids based on the results of your test, and they will be delivered within 3 days. The Care Team is available for ongoing support and adjustments to your devices, ensuring you’re always getting the results you deserve.

Jabra’s Commitment

Jabra Enhance hearing aids are custom-programmed to your unique hearing profile based on test results, ensuring a truly personalized fit. To support you beyond the device, you’ll receive a 3-year virtual care plan from the Audiology Team, giving you remote access to hearing aid adjustments, step-by-step setup walkthroughs, and demonstrations - all from the comfort of your home. Every purchase also includes a 100-day risk-free trial, a free mobile app, and customer support available seven days a week. For added peace of mind, you’ll benefit from 3-year loss and damage protection as well as a 3-year warranty.

Jabra Enhance Features and Tools

Jabra Enhance offers advanced hearing aids backed by a range of excellent features. You can stream audio to your aids from your televisions, smartphone, and other devices with one of the company’s streaming accessories.

In addition, Jabra Enhance's devices are small and cleverly designed, making them virtually invisible when worn correctly. The recharging case is an excellent accessory, enabling you to maintain your devices’ batteries even when you’re on the go. Eight hours worth of charge can be achieved in just 30 minutes, which is excellent.

Another standout feature when compared to low-end hearing aids is Jabra Enhance's personalized service. All devices are fine-tuned according to your hearing test results, ensuring you get the best results possible.

What About the Jabra Enhance App?

The free Jabra Enhance Select app is available on both Android and iOS devices. It’s designed to help you control and customize your hearing aids’ settings, ensuring you’re maintaining the best experience possible. If required, Jabra Enhance audiologists can use the app to optimize your hearing aids. There’s even a “Find my hearing aids” tool that you can use to ensure you never lose them.

Service and Support

Continuous care is available through the Jabra Enhance Select app as part of your hearing aid purchase. You can schedule one-on-one video chats with a qualified specialist, who will be able to make remote changes to your devices’ settings to ensure they’re performing at an optimal level. You can also contact the company via phone, email, online form submission, or social media.

Setup guides and tips are available through the Jabra Enhance Select app, as well as through the company website. There’s also a great FAQ page that provides answers to a range of common questions about payments, hearing health, follow-up care, and more.

How to Get a Refund from Jabra Enhance

Jabra Enhance offers a 100-day return policy on all devices. If you’re not satisfied, you can request a refund by calling or emailing the support team. There are no restocking fees, and the company will even cover return shipping.

Bottom Line

All things considered, Jabra Enhance offers excellent hearing aid solutions for all levels of hearing loss. Its devices are a little expensive, but there’s great value for money on offer for those who can afford the high price tag. Payment plans are also available.

What’s more, you will benefit from the knowledge of a team of hearing specialists. Every purchase comes with a 3-year warranty and 3 years of free customer care, and you will have access to a great app and a range of neat accessories.

products.mainContent:
hear.com Hearing Aid Brands

hear.com offers their own impressive Horizon hearing aid line and a wide range of hearing aids from other world-leading manufacturers. Prices vary depending on the type of device you need and your level of hearing loss.

hear.com

hear.com launched its own Horizon line of hearing aids in 2021. Equipped with state-of-the-art features, the Horizon Mini Go is their top behind-the-ear rechargeable hearing aid that keeps people effortlessly connected and on the go all day. A cutting-edge Speech Boost feature and the 360-degree Panorama mode ensure you hear what’s directly in front of you, and around you, all with a quick, discreet tap of the app. The Go can be charged at home or on the go, has Bluetooth connectivity, and is appropriate for all levels of hearing loss.

Another option is the extremely discreet Horizon Mini X, one of the smallest hearing aids in the world. It sits unnoticeable inside your ear and offers an impressive level of crystal-clear sound. The Mini is best for those with mild to moderate hearing loss who want the best hearing experience in a nearly invisible package. You’ll have access to features like Speech Boost and a Relax Mode for when you’re ready to wind down from it all.

Signia

Signia’s range of hearing aids includes a selection of in-ear and behind-the-ear devices. It uses leading proprietary technology to deliver optimum speech clarity across the board.

Oticon

Oticon has been a leader in the hearing space for over 115 years, and it continues to remain at the forefront of the hearing aid industry. There are 6 product lines available, with solutions for everything from mild to severe hearing loss.

Phonak

Swiss hearing aid manufacturer Phonak is dedicated to delivering the latest in hearing aid technology. It distributes its products through a global network of partners, including hear.com.

Starkey

As one of the USA’s largest hearing aid manufacturers, Starkey naturally offers a wide selection of devices for all types of hearing loss. These include modern AI-based devices that combine hearing aids with various other technologies.

ReSound

ReSound offers a range of hearing aids focusing on “Smart Hearing.” These devices combine mobile technology, audiology, connectivity, and design to ensure you’re getting the best experience possible.

Unitron

Unitron made its name as one of the first companies to digitize hearing aids in the 1990s, and it remains at the forefront of the industry today. Numerous devices are available through hear.com, catering to various budgets and levels of hearing loss.

Widex

Denmark-based hearing aid manufacturer Widex is one of the largest brands in the space. It sells its range of versatile products in more than 100 countries across the globe, including through hear.com’s network of hearing specialists.

Rexton

As the first company to introduce hearing aid features such as Bluetooth connectivity and waterproofing, Rexton remains technologically competitive. It offers a range of in-ear and behind-the-ear devices suited to all levels of hearing loss.

hear.com Additional Services & Products

hear.com works with a network of more than 1,600 partners spread across the United States. Because of this, the selection of additional services and products on offer can vary significantly. In general, you can expect to have access to device-specific accessories, full manufacturer's warranties, and a range of audiologist services. Reach out to hear.com to find out more.

How Do I Purchase from hear.com?

hear.com doesn’t directly sell hearing aids, but they will guide you through the process to make it easy. All devices are sold through the company’s network of hearing specialists, and the hear.com team will connect you to one of their care providers near your home.

To start the supportive process, you just need to complete a short online questionnaire. You’ll be asked a range of questions about why you’re considering purchasing hearing aids, whether you’ve used them in the past, what your budget is, and if you need financing. You’ll then be asked to enter your zip code, phone number, name, and email address.

This information is important because you’ll receive a call from the team to discuss your needs soon after submitting the questionnaire. This enables hear.com to then connect you with one of their local partners for a hearing test.

It’s worth noting that remote video appointments are available with some partners, which will be an attractive option for many people.

hear.com Payment Options

If you decide to use hear.com, you will benefit from various payment options. These will vary depending on the partner you connect with, and there are financing solutions for those with a good credit score.

These payment plans are available directly through hear.com. Interest-free financing is on offer if you pay the entire amount within the first 12 months. Also, 24, 48, and 60-month terms are available as long as you’re able to get credit approval.

Service and Support

If you would like to speak with a hear.com team member, you can reach out via phone or email. Support hours are not listed on the hear.com site but you can also request a callback if you would prefer. There’s a great selection of self-help resources available via the company website, including numerous FAQs, product guides, and a range of informational articles.

It’s worth noting, though, that much of the post-sales support you receive will be from the hear.com partner you’re connected with. They will provide full technical support, and the cost and level of service can vary between partners.

How to Get a Refund from hear.com

hear.com offers a full 45-day money-back guarantee, enabling you to request a refund if you aren’t satisfied with your new hearing aids. Simply call 888-780-3450 to speak with a team member and discuss the best option for returning your hearing aids. Follow the provided instructions, and you should receive a full refund within 2 to 3 days of processing (up to 4 or 5 weeks if you made payments through a financing partner).

The Bottom Line

If you’ve struggled with poor hearing for some time, reaching out to a hear.com specialist could be just what you need. You will be connected with a local hearing expert who will help you develop the best hearing aid solution for your needs. Along with the wide selection of hearing aids on offer, you will benefit from flexible payment options, full manufacturers’ warranties, and a 45-day trial period.

products.mainContent:
Audien Hearing Aid Models

Audien Hearing offers two hearing aid models. They are affordable, rechargeable, and come with all the accessories you need.

One option is the new Atom hearing aid, which features wireless charging. The Atom comes with a dock that charges the hearing aid. Audien says it offers better sound quality, which may be more suitable for people with more profound hearing loss. The Atom costs $189 a pair.

Next, there’s the Atom Pro. At $299 a pair, it’s the most expensive choice from Audien, but this is still significantly cheaper than custom-fitted hearing aids. The Atom Pro, like the Atom, has a docking station for easy recharging. But with the Atom Pro, you can get up to four days of use out of a single charge.

Audien Hearing Additional Services & Products

An additional protection plan (above the standard warranty) provides cover if you lose or break your hearing device. This costs $4/month or $24/year. You will still need to pay for your replacement, albeit at a special, reduced price. Additional charging kits are available for all models. Prices vary, with $24 for an Atom Pro charger with case.

Finally, an accessory pack at $12 includes 12 replacement earbuds, a cleaning brush, a screwdriver, and eight wax guards. You can purchase this on a subscription basis, where a new accessory pack will be sent to you every month for $9/month.

How Do I Purchase Audien Hearing Devices?

Audien Hearing devices are not medical devices regulated and approved by the FDA. Buying Audien Hearing devices is relatively straightforward. You can purchase the devices directly from its website. You don’t need a prescription or have to visit an audiologist. Audien Hearing considers this a major advantage of its products, though its competitors, who do require audiologist visits, are quick to state that they provide more sophisticated hearing devices.

Audien Hearing Payment Options

Payment to Audien Hearing is via a one-time purchase process through the company’s website using a credit card.

No payment plan is available for the devices themselves, but extras such as monthly cleaning kits can be purchased as an ongoing subscription.

Our Breakdown of Audien Hearing Aids

Atom 2

  • Cost: $189
  • Powerful A2 chip
  • 24 hr battery life
  • Charging case


Atom Pro 2

  • Cost: $299
  • Kills 99.9% of bacteria while charging
  • Noise Cancelation
  • Smallest size available
  • Powerful A2 chip
  • 24 hr battery life


Audien Hearing Features and Tools

Audien Hearing devices are relatively simple to use compared to pricier hearing aids. The devices don’t perform any audio manipulation other than amplifying sound. This makes their use in noisy environments inferior to custom-made hearing aids.

The standout feature of Audien Hearing devices, besides the low prices, is their rechargeable nature. You don’t have to change batteries every day. Instead, you need only remember to plug in your earbuds, or sit them on top of the wireless charging dock.

Audien Hearing’s one-size-fits-all approach to hearing aids is certainly a plus for those who don’t want to go through the hassle and expense of getting a hearing aid custom-made. The devices are a legitimate alternative to those that cost over $1,500, as long as you reign in your expectations around sound quality.

Does Audien Hearing Have an App?

Unlike some competitors’ products, Audien Hearing doesn’t include a mobile app for its hearing devices. If you want to check battery levels or adjust volume using a mobile app, you should look elsewhere for your hearing aids.

Audien Service and Support

Customer support is available Monday-Friday between 7am-4pm PT. During this time, you can phone the company or use the live chat system to speak to a representative. Outside of these hours, there is email support only, which has a 24-hour response time.

Online reviews often mention the difficulty of reaching customer support at Audien Hearing, which could be a dealbreaker for many people.

Online support documentation is also sparse, essentially boiling down to four videos that show you how to use each of the devices. Those interested in the specifics of how the devices work are out of luck. Audien Hearing has a blog, but nearly all posts are several years old.

How to Get a Refund from Audien Hearing

Audien Hearing provides a 45-day money-back guarantee and a one-year manufacturer’s warranty. The manufacturer’s warranty offers a complete replacement in the case of a defective product.

To get a refund, you request one through the Audien Hearing website. The support team will provide you with a return shipping label, and you must send the product back from the post office using tracked mail. The shipment must reach Audien’s warehouse 45 days after you received your product, or a refund will not be given. Once the returned product is received by Audien Hearing, your refund will be processed within 3-5 business days.

Online reviews commonly mention problems in getting refunds from Audien Hearing, whether it’s because of a lack of communication or refusal to refund the customer based on a technicality. Because of this, it’s difficult to recommend Audien Hearing to those who value the opportunity to get a full refund easily if the product doesn’t suit them.

The Bottom Line

Audien Hearing provides good hearing amplification devices for your money. They’re easy to use, have several tip sizes, and are rechargeable.

However, don’t buy Audien Hearing devices if you expect them to be direct replacements for more expensive, custom-made hearing devices. The sound quality, while passable, doesn’t compete with a hearing aid specifically designed for your ear canals. The low prices may also affect Audien Hearing’s customer service, as there are plenty of negative customer reviews online to warrant some concern.

Eargo Hearing Aid Models

Eargo has been described as a disruptor in the hearing aid space, selling nearly invisible in-the-ear hearing aids directly to consumers, without the need for an audiologist prescription. The entire process, from hearing screening to fitting, to post-purchase support, is done online.

The hearing aids themselves are modeled after fishing flies, with a set of silicone tips that allow the devices to “float” within the ear canal. Eargo sells four rechargeable models, all with several amplification profiles for different sound environments.

Eargo Max

Price: $1,450

Eargo Max is Eargo’s entry-level hearing aid. In 2018, it was the winner of Time magazine’s Best Inventions of 2018 award. The Eargo Max provides basic Eargo features, such as a choice of sound profiles and a comfortable design featuring silicone Flexi Fibers, but it does not pair with an app. The Eargo Max was designed specifically for patients with mild to moderate, mostly high-frequency hearing loss, so it does not offer amplification for low frequency or severe hearing loss.

Eargo 5

Price: $2,450

The Eargo 5 offers more personalization and a new app that offers hearing screening. It is smaller than the other models and offers better sound quality and Sound Match technology to personalize settings. The charging case features magnets instead of contact pins for easier charging and provides a full charge in 2.5 hours. In the Eargo 5, open petals replace the previous models’ Palms and Fibers.

Eargo 6

Price: $2,950

The newest model from Eargo gives users all of the power of the Eargo 5, with several added benefits. The Eargo 6 uses cutting-edge automatic Sound Adjust technology to accurately identify and reduce background noise as you move between environments. Plus, the 6 model is water-resistant at depths less than 1 meter for up to 30 minutes, meaning you can keep it in place when bathing and swimming.

LINK

Price: $799

The Eargo LINK is an innovative earbud-style OTC hearing aid that combines sleek design with advanced technology. Featuring Bluetooth 5.3, it offers high-quality sound for music and calls, with easy mode switching for different hearing needs. The device provides up to 9 hours of use per charge, with the charging case holding up to 4 additional charges. Rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, the Eargo LINK ensures durability and convenience. It also includes unlimited lifetime support, making it a versatile and user-friendly choice.

Eargo SE

Price: $1,650

The Eargo SE is a virtually invisible CIC hearing aid that offers simplicity and value. It features self-fitting technology via the Sound Match app, allowing customization without clinic visits. With four preset sound modes, it provides up to 16 hours of battery life per charge, and the charging case holds five full charges. Rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, the Eargo SE combines essential Eargo technology, design, and support. It also includes a one-year warranty with unlimited repairs and lifetime remote support.

Eargo 7

Price: $2,950

The Eargo 7 is the most advanced hearing aid from Eargo, designed for virtual invisibility and comfort. Featuring Sound Adjust+ with Clarity Mode, it automatically adapts to your sound environment for clearer conversations. Self-fitting via the Sound Match app allows personalized settings without clinic visits. The rechargeable battery offers up to 16 hours of use, with the case providing up to two days of power. With an IPX7 water-resistance rating and improved noise reduction, Eargo 7 ensures an uninterrupted listening experience. It includes a two-year warranty and lifetime remote support.

Eargo Additional Services & Products

Eargo hearing aids come with the following accessories:

  • A portable charger. Eargo hearing aids are designed to be charged overnight and provide 16 hours of use on one charge. The charger itself lasts one week on a single charge and comes with a power cord.

  • Cleaning accessories. A brush and microfiber cloth are provided to clean the hearing aids before charging each night.

  • Extra wax guards and wax guard changing tool. Eargo hearing aids contain a small internal wax guard, which needs to be replaced every 3-6 months.

  • Silicone tips. Each set of hearing aids comes with a selection of silicone tips to fit a range of canal sizes. The company recommends changing tips every three months to prevent wax buildup.

Additional accessories are available for purchase on the website:

  • Silicone tips: These come in packages of three pairs each for $25.

  • Wax guard replacement tool: for $25, you can purchase a tool with a set of 15 wax filter screens.

The Max and 5 models come with a one-year warranty, while the Eargo 6 has a two-year warranty. All warranties with unlimited repairs and one-time loss or damage coverage. After the warranty period, Eargo will replace a device or charger for $295. The warranty excludes devices purchased from unauthorized distributors, damage from improper handling (including immersion in water), and damage from unauthorized service centers.

How Do I Purchase Eargo Devices?

All Eargo hearing aid models are purchased directly from the company through their website. Customers receive a personal hearing screening and a demonstration with company representatives who are licensed audiology professionals, all through private video appointments. You can request a sample non-working Eargo device to test the comfort level, then after you order the active devices, you will have a 45-day trial period to return them if they don’t work for you.

Eargo Payment Options

Eargo products may be covered through certain insurance companies. Payments can be made using credit, debit, and Health Savings Account cards.

The company offers a payment plan through their finance partner company, Bread. Rates range from 0% to 29.99% APR and are subject to credit approval. For the latest Eargo 6 model, the company advertises payments as low as $94/month over 36 months.

Eargo Features and Tools

  • Eargo's first earbud-style OTC hearing aid with Bluetooth 5.3. Enjoy excellent sound quality and the convenience of Bluetooth for streaming calls or music, and stay connected with just a tap to choose from 4 hearing aid modes

  • Sound Adjust+ with Clarity Mode feature automatically adjusts to your sound environment to deliver crisper speech in noisy environments

  • Several factory-set sound profiles

  • Rechargeable batteries: 16 hours of use on an overnight charge, and 3 hours on a 30-minute quick charge

  • Small size

  • Silicone tips to comfortably hold the hearing aid in the ear canal

  • Smartphone app with Neo 5 and 6 models

  • Noise and wind reduction and feedback cancellation for clear sound quality

  • Remote support options to allow users to receive updates and adjustments from the manufacturer

What About the Eargo App?

The Eargo app is available for free for users of the Neo 5 and 6 models. There are two different versions depending on the model:

  • Eargo 5 app for remotely adjusting Eargo 5 model.

  • Eargo 6 app for the newest Eargo 6 model.

Both apps are available on the Apple App Store for iPhones 5s and later, iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad mini 2 or later, and iPad (October 2012 or later). They are available on Google Play for Android devices running operating system of 6.0 and later. Both apps are intuitive, with a range of useful functions.

The Eargo Neo app allows users to personalize audio settings based on different sound environments (such as restaurants, meetings, and theater). There are four present programs included within the app. Within each program, you can personalize bass and treble settings. The app also allows you to remotely update your hearing aids, provides how-to videos, and offers alerts and reminders for charging and cleaning your devices.

The Eargo app for Eargo 5 and 6 offers Sound Match, a feature that allows the app to customize your hearing aid settings to your level of hearing loss and provides three listening environments. You can manually adjust volume, bass, and treble setting within each environment. The app also allows you to manually adjust the Noise Filter while wearing the hearing aids. It offers alerts, reminders, remote updating, and in-app video calls with Eargo hearing specialists.

Service and Support

For every Eargo product, the company offers “lifetime support” from licensed hearing professionals. The support model is fully remote, with phone, video chat, text, and email contact options.

The Eargo website offers a library of training videos and articles to help with setting up and using the devices, a toll-free phone number, an online “HearingHelper” bot, and an online message center, which states that responses are usually received within a few hours.

The website’s comprehensive FAQ section provides answers to questions about hearing loss, hearing aids, Eargo products, and financing options.

How to Get a Refund from Eargo

Eargo offers a 45-day trial period for their devices. If you return them within this window, you receive a full refund.

The Bottom Line

Eargo hearing aids are relative newcomers to the hearing aid market, with a sales model that allows you to skip a visit to the audiologist. If you have mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss, it may be worth a visit to the website to learn more, request a sample, speak to a hearing specialist, and try them out for 45 days. Rechargeable batteries make them convenient, but be aware that the devices will need to be replaced when the batteries eventually wear out.

At a Glance

Ceretone has emerged as a prominent player in the growing over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aid market in the United States. As of 2025, the brand’s product range includes four primary models:

  • Core One Pro: Invisible-in-canal (IIC), Bluetooth-enabled, rechargeable, IP68 water-resistant, with up to 80 hours of use via case.
  • Core One: Similar to Pro but with slightly fewer features.
  • Advanced Torch: In-the-ear (ITE), compact, with 5 audio programs and IP54 protection.
  • Solid: Behind-the-ear (BTE) model, rechargeable, durable, and affordable.

Each model targets mild to moderate hearing loss, which aligns with FDA guidelines for OTC hearing aids. Features include noise reduction, multi-environment listening modes, and water resistance ratings (IP54 to IP68). Importantly, all Ceretone hearing aids are rechargeable, eliminating the need for disposable batteries, and come with a portable charging case.

How to Get Started

Getting started with Ceretone is designed to be accessible and intuitive. The process is fully online and includes the following steps:

  • Visit the Ceretone Website: Navigate to ceretone.com and select the 'Hearing Products' section.
  • Take the Hearing Test: Use the free online test to determine product suitability.
  • Choose a Model: Compare the Core One Pro, Core One, Advanced Torch, and Solid models using the brand’s comparison chart.
  • Order Online: Place an order directly via the website. Each product includes a 60-day risk-free trial.
  • Use the App (for compatible models): For models like the Core One Pro, users can download the Bluetooth app to control volume and settings.

There is no need for prescriptions, hearing exams, or in-person consultations, consistent with FDA OTC regulations.

Special Features

Ceretone’s hearing aids include a variety of notable features, depending on the model:

  • Bluetooth 5.0: Found in premium models like the Core One Pro, this allows streaming from smartphones and controlling audio settings via app.
  • Rechargeable Batteries: All models are rechargeable. The high-end models provide up to 80 hours with the case, significantly reducing maintenance.
  • IP Ratings: Products have water-resistance ratings ranging from IP54 to IP68, offering protection from moisture and dust.
  • Noise Reduction: All models feature adaptive noise suppression and feedback cancellation.
  • Multi-Program Modes: Most devices come with 4–5 listening programs, adaptable for different environments such as indoors, outdoors, or noisy settings.

Customer Service

Ceretone offers a multi-channel customer support service:

  • Phone Support: (866) 283-4262
  • Email/Online Support: support@ceretone.com
  • Live Chat: Available on the website

The brand’s support has received positive feedback for being responsive, helpful, and willing to offer replacements or refunds quickly.

Is it Reliable?

Ceretone is a reliable option for adults seeking an affordable and discreet hearing aid without requiring a prescription. While it does not offer audiologist fittings or custom programming, the inclusion of Bluetooth control, rechargeable batteries, and multi-environment settings provides convenience and functionality.

Customer reviews highlight ease of use, comfort, and effective amplification for everyday activities. The 60-day risk-free trial also adds a layer of reliability, giving customers time to evaluate the product without long-term commitment.

How to Cancel or Pause a Subscription

Ceretone does not operate on a subscription model. All hearing aid products are one-time purchases. Returns can be made within 60 days of receipt under the risk-free trial policy. Customers must contact customer service to initiate a return and receive a return label.

Is There an App?

Yes, select Ceretone models like the Core One Pro offer a Bluetooth companion app compatible with iOS and Android. Through the app, users can:

  • Adjust volume
  • Change program settings
  • Switch between listening environments

The app simplifies user interaction and enhances personalization. However, it is only supported on select models, which is worth considering during purchase.

Pricing and Plans

Ceretone’s hearing aids are competitively priced within the OTC category:

  • Core One Pro: $389.99 (was $699.99)
  • Core One: $349.99 (was $699.99)
  • Advanced Torch: $249.99 (was $399.99)
  • Solid: $199.99 (was $329.99)

All prices are for a pair and include accessories and a charging case. Free shipping and a 60-day trial are standard with all purchases. There are no hidden fees or recurring charges.

Bottom Line

Ceretone offers a compelling solution for adults in the U.S. with mild to moderate hearing loss. Its hearing aids are FDA-registered, affordable, and feature-rich, with Bluetooth integration, rechargeability, and discreet form factors. The availability of multiple styles and price points enhances its appeal across different user needs.

While professional fitting and audiologist support are not included, the product range still stands out for convenience, trial flexibility, and customer service. For those seeking OTC hearing aids without complex fittings or appointments, Ceretone represents a sound, value-oriented choice.

MDHearing Hearing Aid Models

MDHearing has been selling FDA-registered hearing aids direct to the consumer for over a decade. These devices are affordable and easy to use. The company sells three behind-the-ear models, all designed to meet the needs of most adults with uncomplicated mild to moderate hearing loss.

While all MDHearing devices provide a level of user-driven customization, they are not individually programmed by an audiologist. Instead, you will choose among four preset sound environments and manually adjust volume levels within them. For more advanced models, you will find added “smart” features and more ways to personalize your hearing experience.

Air

Price: $299

The Air is MDHearing’s entry-level model. It offers the standard brand features, including four preset hearing environments, a volume dial, a basic level of background noise cancellation, and feedback cancellation (which removes the whistling effect found in older hearing aid models). It uses disposable batteries, and each pair comes with a year’s supply.

Neo

Price: $299/pair

MDHearing has come out with a hearing aid model made for those seeking the smallest and most lightweight device possible. NEO ends up being a super discreet hearing aid, that looks almost invisible in the ear. The device is rechargeable through a charging case, which is reminiscent in design to today's wireless headphones. The battery lasts for more than 17 hours of high-quality hearing.

Volt

Price: $399/pair

For $200 more per pair, the Volt includes several upgrades over the Air. Intelligent background noise cancellation uses advanced algorithms to fine-tune background noise response for an improved listening experience. This model also includes dual-directional microphones, which allow the device to distinguish between sounds you want to hear – like conversations in front of you – from those you don’t, like sounds behind you. The Volt is the only MDHearing model that is rechargeable.

Volt Max

Price: $699/pair

At almost double the price of the Volt, the Volt Max model includes some great features, like an app to create a hearing map to drive a more customized, automatic hearing experience. Rather than fiddling with buttons and dials on the hearing aid itself, you can adjust settings on your app and allow the hearing aid to automatically switch between sound settings while you’re wearing them. In many ways, the Volt Max is an improvement over the Volt, but it uses disposable batteries. Like the Volt, it includes intelligent noise reduction and dual-directional microphones.

MDHearing Additional Services & Products

All MDHearing devices come with a one-year warranty covering defects in materials and workmanship. You can purchase additional coverage through their MDShield Protection Plan, which costs $9.99/month for Air and Volt models and $14.99/month for Volt Max. The plan can be canceled at any time. MDShield covers damage not included in the warranty, such as pet damage, battery corrosion, and accidental destruction. The plan does not cover loss, theft, or damage from unauthorized repairs.

When you purchase a pair of MDHearing devices, you will receive a year’s supply of batteries (for Air and Volt Max models), or a charger (for the Volt model). MDHearing sells a variety of additional tools and accessories on their website, including tubing replacement kits, batteries, cleaning tools, and hearing aid dehumidifiers.

MDHearing offers a free hearing test on their website. This test works with headphones and takes about eight minutes to complete. It doesn’t replace a thorough audiologist workup, but it can help to verify any hearing loss you think you might have and provide insight to help you determine if MDHearing devices might work for you.

How Do I Purchase MDHearing Devices?

While a hearing test is not required to purchase MDHearing devices, the company will review the results of your existing hearing tests if you have them, and they offer a free online hearing screening to help inform your purchase decision.

The hearing aids can be purchased online or by calling the company’s toll-free number. The entire ordering process is performed directly with the company, eliminating the need for an audiologist’s prescription.

MDHearing Payment Options

MDHearing accepts traditional online payment options (credit and debit cards, PayPal), and accepts checks or money orders by postal mail. The company offers a financing option through Affirm. For a $400 purchase, Affirm advertises an estimated payment plan of $33.33/month for 12 months if you qualify for 0% APR.

Oticon Hearing Aid Models

Oticon offers 11 different series of hearing aids and dozens of models to suit every budget and type of hearing impairment. The company makes both behind-the-ear (BTE) and receiver-in-channel (RIC) hearing aids, as well as devices specifically for children. Oticon is at the leading edge of hearing aid technology and typically releases peer-reviewed research with each new model to back up its claims about the quality of its devices.

It’s worth noting that most Oticon hearing aids are compatible with the company’s CROS technology, which optimizes for hearing loss in one ear. Adding CROS to any hearing aid increases the price by about $1,000.

More

The More hearing aid is Oticon’s newest device. It includes an onboard deep neural network that’s been trained on over 12 million sounds, enabling the hearing aid to denoise your environment and amplify speech during conversations. Compared to the Opn S, Oticon’s second-newest hearing aid model, the More delivers 30% more sound.

This hearing aid is best for people with moderate hearing loss who want the highest-quality conversations and don’t mind using a BTE receiver. The More costs $2,761.

Opn, Opn S & Opn Play

The Opn and Opn S have 3 hearing aid models each, including both BTE and RIC hearing aids. The devices in each series eliminate noise using Oticon’s BrainHearing technology, which is an earlier iteration of the technology used in the More. OpnS hearing aids use a slightly more advanced version of the BrainHearing algorithm and offer 15% better speech understanding than Opn series hearing aids.

The Opn and Opn S are most suitable for people with moderate to severe hearing loss who prefer an RIC over a BTE hearing aid. The Opn S RIC model costs $3,568, while the Opn RIC model costs $3,250. In addition, Oticon offers 4 Opn Play models, which are designed for children, starting at $2,300.

Xceed & Xceed Play

The Xceed is a line of high-powered hearing aids designed for people with severe hearing loss. These devices offer a 360-degree microphone so that you’re not limited to only hearing what’s in front of you. They also use sound optimization technology to eliminate static and whistling even at high amplification volumes.

The Xceed series includes 3 BTE models, which range in price from $2,609 to $3,538. Oticon also offers 2 Xceed Play hearing aids, which are designed for children with severe hearing loss and start at $2,500

Ruby

The Ruby hearing aid lineup consists of 5 BTE and RIC hearing aids that use Oticon’s older Velox sound processing system. While these hearing aids lack the advanced noise cancellation of the Opn and More series, they are much more affordable. Ruby series hearing aids start at $1,733.

Siya

Siya is a series of 9 different hearing aids that, like Ruby devices, use Oticon’s Velox sound processing technology. What differentiates the Siya series is that it includes a number of in-the-canal hearing aids. The smallest of these go deep inside your ear canal and are virtually invisible when you’re wearing them. Siya hearing aids start at $1,818.

Dynamo

The Dynamo is a single hearing aid model that is Oticon’s most powerful option for people with severe hearing loss. This BTE hearing aid is designed to amplify noise without sacrificing clarity and uses Oticon’s BrainHearing technology to specifically transmit speech. The Dynamo costs $1,990.

Sensei & Sensei SP

The Sensei series is a line of 3 BTE and RIC hearing aids designed specifically for children. They include BrainHearing technology for clarity and Bluetooth connectivity for connecting to smart educational devices. In addition, Sensei hearing aids are fully water-resistant. They start at $1,395.

For children with severe hearing loss, Oticon also makes the Sensei SP (Super Power) hearing aid. This uses the same technology as the Sensei, but offers greater amplification and is only available as a BTE model. The Sensei SP costs $1,595.

Oticon Additional Services & Products

Oticon offers a 2-year manufacturer’s warranty on all hearing aids, plus a 1-year warranty for loss and damage. You’ll need to bring your hearing aid to an Oticon audiologist, and they can offer a replacement part immediately or ship your hearing aids back to Oticon for replacement.

Oticon also offers ConnectClip and ConnectLine devices to help you make the most of your hearing aids. ConnectClip enables you to make phone calls wirelessly from your smartphone and includes a built-in microphone to transmit your speech. ConnectLine is a television adapter that lets you connect your hearing aids directly to your television’s audio feed.

How Do I Purchase Oticon Devices?

To purchase Oticon hearing aids, you’ll need to schedule a hearing test with a local audiologist who sells Oticon products so that you can get a prescription for your device. The company has thousands of dealers across the US, with at least one in every state.

Oticon Payment Options

Your options to pay for Oticon hearing aids will depend on the local audiologist you purchase them through. Oticon itself doesn’t offer information about payment plans nor any insurance policies that cover its devices.

Oticon Features and Tools

The number one thing that differentiates Oticon hearing aids from other manufacturers is the company’s use of noise-canceling technology. The new More hearing aid has a built-in neural network trained on over 12 million sounds, enabling it to decide what noise to amplify and what to eliminate. That reduces the effort of following conversations and results in 15% better speech understanding compared to the Opn S.

While the Opn S and older models don’t have a neural network, they also offer Oticon’s BrainHearing technology. This scans your surroundings 100 times per second to differentiate noise from conversation and eliminate chatter.

What About the Oticon App?

Nearly all of Oticon’s hearing aids can connect via Bluetooth to the Oticon ON mobile app. This free app is available for both iOS and Android devices, including the Apple Watch.

With the Oticon ON app, you can adjust your hearing aid’s volume, keep track of how frequently you use your hearing aid, and stream music or audio directly to your hearing device. Oticon ON also integrates with IFTTT, which lets you set up ‘if this then that’ controls for all of the internet-connected devices in your home. So, for example, you can program your hearing aid to turn on whenever the television turns on.

Service and Support

Oticon doesn’t provide direct support for customers. The company offers documentation for all of its hearing aids, including user guides, but that’s about it. If you need help with your device, you’ll need to speak with your local audiologist or another audiologist that sells Oticon products.

How to Get a Refund from Oticon

Oticon encourages audiologists to offer a risk-free trial for its hearing aids, although the length and details of this trial vary by provider. If you want to get a refund, you’ll need to go through the audiologist from whom you bought your Oticon hearing aid.

Bottom Line

Oticon’s hearing aids are premium devices that offer cutting-edge technology like deep learning-based noise cancellation and automatic sound optimization. The company has models for every type of hearing impairment, including devices specific for children and hearing loss in one ear only. While visiting an audiologist to purchase Oticon hearing aids can be a hassle, the company’s network of thousands of dealers across the US means that support is always nearby when you need it.

articles.metaTitle: The Top 10 Must-Haves: Best Hearing Aid Accessories of 2026
articles.metaDescription: Are you a hearing aid user, or have you recently discovered you’ll need to start using one? Read our round-up of 10 essential hearing aid accessories.
articles.title: Top 10 Must-Have Hearing Aid Accessories
articles.subtitle: April 3, 2024
articles.summary: Whether you’ve been living with hearing loss for years or only recently noticed changes, the right hearing aids - and the right accessories - can open doors. With a few smart add‑ons, everyday moments become easier: catching a joke at a busy dinner, following directions on a conference call, or enjoying a film without cranking the volume.
articles.mainContent:
Many accessories are purely practical, while others add comfort, convenience, and durability to your setup. Some items (like power and cleaning tools) are close to essential. Others can transform how you listen in specific situations, from windy walks to echoey meeting rooms. Below is a simple, real‑world guide to 10 accessory types that can make day‑to‑day life far easier.

Answer a few quick questions to find the right hearing aids for you Get Started

1. Hearing aid cases

A sturdy case protects your hearing aids from dust, drops, and moisture when they’re not in your ears. It also gives you a clean spot to place your devices during showers, workouts, or naps, reducing the chance of misplacing them. While a case alone isn’t a hygiene solution, it helps keep everything organized so you can stick to a simple clean‑and‑store routine.

Cases matter at home and on the go, especially if you have small children or curious pets who might tamper with delicate parts. A well‑designed case often includes compartments for spare domes, wax guards, and a small brush. If you’re frequently outdoors, consider a hard‑shell option with a secure latch; if you travel, look for a case that also fits your charger or drying capsule.

2. Hearing aid retention wires

Because hearing aids are small, the worry of losing them is real - particularly for active users and new wearers. Retention cords (sometimes called safety lines) add a lightweight tether between your hearing aids and your clothing to reduce the chance of a drop turning into a loss.

Typical sets include flexible loops that attach to the aids and a small clip for your collar, shirt, or hat. They’re especially useful during gardening, sports, hiking, or any activity where quick movements, helmets, or hats might nudge a device out of place. Many versions are barely noticeable once clipped and can be removed in seconds when you’re back indoors.

3. Hearing aid earbuds (OTC options)

Earbud‑style over‑the‑counter (OTC) hearing aids are designed for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing difficulties and can be purchased without a prescription. Their draw is straightforward: easy access, familiar earbud styling, and simple setup. Some models include basic app controls so you can fine‑tune sound in common environments like restaurants or at home.

Because everyone’s hearing profile is different, OTC options aren’t a substitute for a professional evaluation—especially if you have sudden changes, pain, or tinnitus. Still, for many adults who want a simple starting point, earbud‑style OTC devices can be a practical way to improve clarity for conversation, TV, and calls. If you try one and still struggle, book a hearing check to explore fitted, prescription devices.

4. Hearing aid chargers

If you’ve ever had your device fade during a meeting or school pickup, you know how valuable a reliable charger is. Most modern rechargeable hearing aids sit in a compact dock that tops up the built‑in battery - many reach a full charge in about three hours, and some offer quick‑charge options that give you several hours of use in a shorter window.

Disposable zinc‑air batteries remain common, and performance varies by size and usage. Many users get several days from smaller sizes and up to a couple of weeks from larger ones, depending on streaming and volume. Whatever you use, keep power supplies handy: a bedside charger for routine, a travel case for trips, and a couple of spare disposables in your bag just in case. Store batteries dry and at room temperature - no refrigeration needed.

5. Hearing aid cleaning kits

Clean devices sound better and are more comfortable. Most kits include a soft brush, dry cloth, wax loop or pick, and sometimes a small vent/tube cleaner. A few minutes of routine care helps prevent wax from blocking ports and keeps microphones and receivers working as intended.

A good habit is to wipe the aids each night, clear visible debris around the domes or earmolds, and swap wax guards as instructed by your manufacturer or provider. If your original kit goes missing, replacements are affordable and widely available. For in‑ear styles, keep a few extra domes and wax filters on hand so you’re never stuck waiting for a replacement part to arrive.

6. Hearing aid carrying bags

When you need to remove your devices - for swimming, gym sessions, or a windy beach walk - how you carry them matters. A small, padded bag or hard‑shell case reduces the risk of knocks and moisture, while a zip pocket keeps tools and spare parts together. Consider a bag with separate compartments for microphones, streamers, chargers, and cables to prevent scratching and tangles.

If you travel frequently, choose a case with space for universal plugs or a power bank. For day trips, a compact pouch that slides into a jacket or handbag is enough. The goal is simple: keep your gear protected and easy to find so you can put the aids back in quickly and confidently when you’re ready.

7. Bluetooth streamers for hearing aids

Bluetooth connectivity lets many hearing aids pair with phones, tablets, and TVs for calls, music, and video. Newer aids often connect directly to recent smartphones, while others use a streamer - a small intermediary device that helps the audio handshake between your hearing aids and the source.

Streamers can also improve reliability in tricky environments (think long distances, older TVs, or laptops that don’t support the right protocol). If you enjoy convenient, app‑based control, brands such as Jabra offer TV streamers and smartphone apps that make it easy to adjust volume, switch programs, and manage settings without touching the devices themselves. Check your model’s compatibility before purchasing to make sure you’ll get the features you want.

8. Remote microphones for hearing aids

Conversation in noise is a common challenge - even with great hearing aids. A remote microphone clips to a talker’s clothing or sits near a sound source and wirelessly sends clearer speech to your aids. It’s a small change that can make a big difference in busy restaurants, lecture halls, or open‑plan offices.

You can also place a remote mic by the TV or conference speaker to reduce echo and distance effects. Some models integrate into brand ecosystems alongside streamers and apps, letting you control mic directionality or sensitivity. If you regularly attend meetings, classes, or social events, a remote mic is one of the highest‑impact add‑ons you can buy.

9. Hearing aid remote controls

Touching small buttons on your ears isn’t always convenient. Remote controls and mobile apps let you change volume, switch programs, or mute sound discreetly. Handheld remotes slip into a pocket or bag and are simple to operate without looking. App controls add extras like battery status, find‑my‑hearing‑aid tools, and location‑based memories.

If you prefer smartphone control, look for brands that support robust apps and accessories. For example, Jabra offers app‑based adjustments for compatible models, so you can fine‑tune sound before a presentation or dial down background noise at a party without pausing the conversation.

10. Hearing aid dryer

Moisture is one of the most common threats to hearing aid performance. Electronic dryers use gentle heat and airflow to remove moisture from ports and tubing, helping prevent intermittent sound or corrosion over time. Place your aids in the dryer at night, and they’ll be ready to go in the morning.

If you want something even simpler, desiccant dehumidifiers use moisture‑absorbing pellets or gel. They’re inexpensive, portable, and don’t require power - handy for travel or as a backup. Some electronic units add UV light to reduce surface bacteria inside the chamber, but you should still wipe visible debris before drying for the best result.

Summary

Discovering a hearing problem can feel daunting, but smart accessories make the journey easier. A protective case and cleaning kit keep your devices in shape. Chargers and spare batteries ensure you’re powered up when it counts. Streamers, remote microphones, and remotes help you hear confidently in the places that matter - restaurants, classrooms, offices, and living rooms.

If you damage or misplace parts, most items - domes, wax guards, cords, and cases - are easy to replace. And if you’re unsure which accessories fit your exact model, a quick check with your hearing‑care provider or the manufacturer’s site will point you in the right direction. Whatever you choose, start simple, build from your needs, and enjoy clearer, more comfortable listening every day.

articles.title: Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids: Are They Right for You?
articles.subtitle: April 3, 2024
articles.summary: In August 2022, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) finalized a rule establishing a new category of over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids. Adults aged 18 and older with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss can now purchase OTC hearing aids in stores or online - no prescription, medical exam, or professional fitting required.
articles.mainContent:
This change is expected to expand access to high-quality hearing care while also driving innovation and lowering costs, potentially saving consumers an average of $2,800 to $3,000 per pair.

Who OTC hearing aids are for (and not for)

OTC hearing aids are air‑conduction devices for adults with perceived mild‑to‑moderate hearing loss. They are not for children or for people with severe/profound loss or “red‑flag” symptoms (e.g., ear pain or drainage, sudden hearing loss, one‑sided loss, persistent dizziness). If you have red‑flag symptoms or more significant loss, see a licensed hearing care professional (ideally an ENT or audiologist).

OTC vs. prescription hearing aids

OTC hearing aids do not replace prescription hearing aids. Prescription devices remain available and are generally recommended for more complex or severe loss. Importantly, the 2022 rule repealed the prior federal medical‑evaluation requirement for adults; states may still regulate provider practices for prescription devices. Any hearing aid that does not meet the OTC requirements is a prescription device.

Signs of Mild‑to‑Moderate Hearing Loss

An OTC hearing aid might be right for you if you have mild‑to‑moderate hearing loss. Here are some of the most common signs:

  • Often struggle to hear people in noisy places or group conversations.

  • Frequently turn up the TV or radio volume.

  • Find that speech sounds muffled or unclear.

  • Have trouble hearing on the phone.

  • Often need to ask others to repeat themselves.

If you’re not sure about your level of hearing loss, seeing a hearing professional for a quick check‑up can be very helpful. And if you experience ear pain, drainage, sudden hearing changes, hearing loss in only one ear, or dizziness, see a licensed hearing professional before buying an OTC device.

Key safety and labeling requirements

OTC hearing aids have to meet strict FDA safety rules. They must limit how loud they can get to prevent hearing damage, include a way for you to adjust the volume, and meet quality standards for sound and background noise. Every package must also include clear, easy‑to‑read labels with safety warnings (such as when to see a doctor), the manufacturer’s contact details, and any information about returns or warranties.

Types and common features

OTC products come in familiar styles (e.g., in‑ear, behind‑the‑ear/receiver‑in‑canal). Many models offer app‑based setup, preset or self‑fitting options, Bluetooth audio/phone streaming, directional microphones, noise reduction, and rechargeable batteries. Features vary - check manufacturer specifications and instructions.

Costs and where to buy

Prices vary widely by brand, features, and services. At launch, major U.S. retailers and pharmacies (e.g., Walgreens, CVS, Walmart, Best Buy) offered OTC hearing aids with examples ranging from about $199 to $3,000 per pair. Federal estimates suggested potential savings up to ~$3,000 per pair versus traditional channels, but actual savings depend on what you buy and any services you add. To see how current models compare on features and prices visit our OTC hearing aid comparison guide.

Insurance and Medicare

Original Medicare (Part A/B) does not cover hearing aids or routine fitting exams. Some Medicare Advantage (Part C) and commercial plans may include hearing benefits (coverage, allowances, and networks vary by plan), so check your policy before you buy.

Why earlier access matters

Many people wait about seven years after noticing symptoms to seek help. Untreated hearing loss is linked with social isolation, depression, falls, and cognitive decline. Recent randomized evidence suggests that treating hearing loss slowed cognitive decline over three years in older adults at higher risk, though it did not show a preventive effect across all participants. Treating hearing loss improves communication and quality of life even when cognitive benefits are uncertain.

Questions to ask before you buy

  • What is the return window, trial period, and warranty (if any)?

  • Is the device preset or self‑fitting? Are there clear instructions/app tutorials?

  • Do you need a smartphone or computer for setup or adjustments?

  • How do you adjust volume and other settings?

  • Are they water/sweat‑resistant?

  • Battery: rechargeable vs. disposable; expected runtime.

  • Do they support Bluetooth?

  • What customer support channels are available (email/chat/phone)?

  • If buying in a store, does staff provide basic counseling on OTC hearing aids?

How to get started

  • Consider a hearing check (in‑person or validated app‑based screening) to set a baseline.

  • Review FDA “red‑flag” symptoms; see a clinician first if any apply.

  • Compare models and features against your needs (noise reduction, rechargeability, app control).

  • Buy from a reputable retailer with a clear return window, and wear the devices consistently during the trial.

  • If benefit is limited, consult an audiologist/ENT to consider prescription options or additional rehabilitation.

Bottom line

OTC hearing aids are a lower‑barrier option for many adults with mild‑to‑moderate hearing loss. They’re widely available without a prescription and must meet FDA safety and labeling standards. Use the return window to confirm real‑world benefit - and seek professional care promptly for red‑flag symptoms or if your hearing needs are more complex.
